title: stochastic-anchor-mosaic-doodle
content:
Purpose:
- Quick personal scratchpad for the 'stochastic anchor mosaic' idea; trying to build a small, reusable prompt primitive that mixes hard anchors (explicit instructions) with soft exemplars (few-shot fragments) that can be stochastically toggled per request to improve robustness and reduce brittle dependencies on a single exemplar ordering.

Motivation / hypothesis:
- Single exemplar ordering + static anchor often overfits to phrasing; we observe brittle flips in style/regression when token budgets or truncation changes.
- By treating exemplars/anchor fragments as a mosaic (set of small shards) and stochastically sampling which shards are included and in what order, we can:
  * surface more semantic coverage (diverse phrasing),
  * detect anchor fragility (if an anchor shard is critical for correctness),
  * implicitly ensemble within a single call to reduce hallucination spikes.

High-level plan (quick):
- Implement 3 primitive types: HARD_ANCHOR (always present, short), SOFT_SHARD (few-shot micro-exemplar, 1-2 sentences), CONTROL_TOKEN (format hint / TTL).
- Experiment configs: mosaic_size = {2,4,8}, shard_length = {8-30 tokens}, sampling = {uniform, weighted-by-coverage}, reorder = {true,false}.
- Metrics: exact-match on structured extraction, semantic-similarity (embedding cosine) for open answers, token consumption, failure-mode labels (missing-field, hallucinated-field, malformed-output).

Minimal prompt primitive grammar (working notation):
- <<HARD_ANCHOR>> - single-line instruction, imperative, max 30 chars.
- <<SHARD_i>> - micro-exemplar. contains: short context -> user query -> desired concise output.
- <<CONTROL>> - e.g., "Format: JSON single object. TTL: 80 tokens"

Example (mosaic_size=3, reorder=true):
<<HARD_ANCHOR>>
You are a concise extraction agent. Return exactly the requested fields in JSON.

<<SHARD_A>>
Context: Email about subscription change.
Q: "Cancel subscription and refund prorated amount"
A: {"action":"cancel", "refund":"prorated"}

<<SHARD_B>>
Context: Support chat: billing dispute.
Q: "I was charged twice"
A: {"action":"investigate_charge", "amount_disputed":true}

<<SHARD_C>>
Context: user asks for upgrade.
Q: "Upgrade plan to Pro"
A: {"action":"upgrade", "target_plan":"Pro"}

<<CONTROL>>
Format: single-line JSON, fields: action, metadata (optional). Max tokens: 70

---
Notes on few-shot shards:
- Shards should be minimal and self-contained. Avoid pronouns that leak cross-shard dependences.
- Intentionally include a couple of near-duplicate shards to test redundancy.
- Include adversarial shard where exemplar has slightly different schema (e.g., uses "operation" vs "action") to test schema robustness.

Failure cases to collect (label taxonomy):
- missing_field: omitted required key
- renamed_field: uses synonym key (operation) instead of expected (action)
- extra_hallucinated_field: invents non-existent metadata
- type_mismatch: returns string when expected boolean/enum
- format_error: not JSON / trailing text
- overfitting_to_shard_order: correct only when shard X is first

Quick experimental matrix (notes):
- Baseline: HARD_ANCHOR + 2 fixed shards (static ordering) -> run on 1k queries.
- Mosaic-uniform: HARD_ANCHOR + sample 4 shards uniform no reorder.
- Mosaic-weighted: sample 4 shards weighted by coverage score (coverage = how many unique slot-values represented).
- Mosaic-reorder: sample 4 shards shuffle order each request.

Preliminary expectations:
- uniform/reorder reduces overfitting but may slightly increase missing_field because some shards with the explicit slot example might be dropped.
- weighted sampling should balance precision/recall by keeping high-value shards.

Sample few-shot shard bank (short snippets):
- SHARD_1: "Context: refund request. Q: "I want my money back for last month" A: {"action":"refund", "scope":"last_month"}"
- SHARD_2: "Context: move account. Q: "Transfer my data to new team" A: {"action":"transfer", "target":"team_account"}"
- SHARD_3: "Context: billing charge question. Q: "Charged $45 twice" A: {"action":"investigate_charge", "amount":45}"
- SHARD_4: "Context: plan cancel but keep data. Q: "Cancel billing but retain data" A: {"action":"cancel", "preserve_data":true}"
- SHARD_5 (adversarial): "Context: same intent, different key. Q: "Stop subscription" A: {"operation":"cancel", "refund":"none"}"
- SHARD_6 (format trap): "Context: verbose answer. Q: "I want to downgrade" A: action: downgrade; note: user wants cheaper tier"

Quick test queries (small list for manual inspection):
- Q1: "Please cancel my Pro subscription and prorate refund" -> expect: {action: cancel, refund: prorated}
- Q2: "I have been billed twice for April" -> expect: {action: investigate_charge, amount_disputed: true}
- Q3: "Move my workspace data to acme-inc" -> expect: {action: transfer, target: acme-inc}

Data collection / telemetry bits to attach per-call:
- shards_used: [list of shard ids] (we will log tokenized ids server-side)
- anchor_hash: hashed HARD_ANCHOR text version (to detect small edits)
- sampling_seed: for reproducibility
- model: model_name + quantization_profile
- latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_estimate
- output_label(s): failure_case if any

Small debugging heuristics:
- If renamed_field occurs >10% for queries referencing slot X -> add a canonicalization shard that maps synonyms to canonical key names (mini prompt with examples mapping "operation"->"action").
- If format_error spikes when shard_length > 24 tokens -> reduce shard verbosity or enforce stricter CONTROL token.

Edge experiments (ideas for later):
- cross-shard priming: have 1 shard that is a tiny schema definition and sample it with low probability (0.1) to see if schema reminders reduce rename errors.
- annealing schedule: early in a session sample more shards (higher mosaic_size), later reduce to speed up / token savings.
- shard meta-tags: attach small tokens like [SLOT:billing] and test if model learns to prefer shards with matching tags when query contains those keywords.

Quick notes (to-self):
- Try both streaming and non-streaming variants; streaming might see partial KV cache benefits for long shard banks.
- Watch out for token miscounts when CONTROL includes 'Max tokens' hint - model sometimes ignores but token accounting still applies.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to best compute 'coverage' score cheaply in the client? (approx via embeddings cluster count vs exact slot heuristics)
- Should we normalize shard phrasing (canonical verbs) or keep diversity to avoid overfitting?
- Which models to run first: base-7b quant vs 13b? Start with 7b for faster iteration.

Run log (scratch):
- 2026-01-05: quick smoke - mosaic_size=4 uniform on 200 samples with model-redwood-7b-q2; observed rename_field ~12%, missing_field ~5%.
- 2026-01-07: added canonicalization shard -> rename_field dropped to 4% but occasional extra_hallucinated_field increased from 2%->5% (maybe canonical shard too prescriptive).

Ideas for packaging as reusable primitive:
- Provide a small client helper: build_mosaic(shard_bank, hard_anchor, config) -> deterministic list + sampling_seed.
- Expose telemetry hooks: log_shard_selection + canonicalization_suggestions.

Small checklist before sharing with Lina: 
- [ ] clean up shard bank and remove free-text traps
- [ ] add 50 curated adversarial examples (rename, format, hallucination)
- [ ] write short README usage snippet for the library (3 lines)
- [ ] open PR with helper and minimal tests (link above)

Slack / comms notes:
- Thread: #prompt-studies anchored-mosaic. Ping Lina + Jonah for early review.
- Mention in weekly DEX sync if numbers look promising.

End of scratchpad. Keep this intentionally messy; will extract a cleaner PR draft once we have 1k-run results.
